sites.rationale: C-terminus not extracellular (topology 'I' at residue L) and no accessible N-terminus — C-terminal snorkel presents the tag on the surface via a TM-snorkeling linker (fallback: no natively accessible terminus)
ordered surface loop (8 aa): pLDDT>=70, DSSP loop/turn, exposed junction residue (max RSA), indel-tolerant, 3D-clear of features

literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1, L2) describe the same construct: full-length human TMEM86B with a C-terminal 6x myc tag expressed in HEK293T cells. Per the authoritative topology landmarks, the C-terminus (residues 219–226) is intracellular; the tag therefore faces the cytoplasm and does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site. The four extracellular loops of TMEM86B (residues 41–46, 94–96, 141–147, 190–196) are all extremely short (3–7 residues) and directly flanked by TM helices with zero residues of margin from TM boundaries, but — critically — neither ledger line reports any insertion in any of these loops. No ledger evidence grounds an extracellular tag site, so zero sites are reported.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal 6x myc tag on full-length TMEM86B (pEXPR-IBA103 vector); the C-terminus (residues 219–226) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
